definitions.explanation: The transition from a probationary or trial period to permanent, full employment status. In Japanese companies, new employees typically undergo a trial period before receiving official permanent status.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試用期間|しようきかん}→試用期間：15675_shiyoukikan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経|へ}て→経る：13876_heru⟧{本採用|ほんさいよう}になった。
examples.english: After the probationary period, I became a permanent employee.

examples.japanese: ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧か{月|げつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試用期間|しようきかん}→試用期間：15675_shiyoukikan⟧⟦{後|ご}→後：30157_go⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{決|き}まる→決まる：01233_kimaru⟧。
examples.english: Permanent employment is decided after a three-month probationary period.

examples.japanese: {本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦されれば→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{社会保険|しゃかいほけん}→社会保険：18894_shakaihoken⟧や⟦{賞与|しょうよ}→賞与：04694_shouyo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対象|たいしょう}→対象：03393_taishou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Once permanently hired, you become eligible for social insurance and bonuses.

notes:
USAGE:
Contrasts with ⟦{試用|しよう}→試用：23966_shiyou⟧ (probationary/trial) employment. In Japanese companies, most new hires go through a ⟦{試用期間|しようきかん}→試用期間：15675_shiyoukikan⟧ (probationary period), typically three to six months, before {本採用|ほんさいよう} is confirmed. {本採用|ほんさいよう} means the employee is now a ⟦{正社員|せいしゃいん}→正社員：13194_seishain⟧ (full-time permanent employee) with all associated benefits.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Also used as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb: {本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to hire permanently). The passive form {本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be permanently hired) is common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become permanently employed
- {本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{決|き}まる→決まる：01233_kimaru⟧: permanent hire is confirmed
- {本採用|ほんさいよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見送|みおく}る→見送る：04240_miokuru⟧: to defer/decline permanent hire
